newsitem.title: INDIA: India ends ban on petrochemical borrowings.
newsitem.headline: India ends ban on petrochemical borrowings.

text.p: The Indian government said on Wednesday that a cabinet committee has lifted a five-year-old ban on borrowing from public financial institutions for petrochemical cracker projects.

The government said in a statement that the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs "today has approved a proposal for lifting the ban imposed in the letters of intent and industrial licences issued to various parties for cracker projects on borrowings from public financial institutions".
A government spokesman said that to date, the ban has applied to 11 large petrochemical cracker projects, each involving investments of some 40 billion to 50 billion rupees.
Cracker plants break up naphtha or natural gas into basic building blocks of petrochemical products.
The statement said the ban had been in effect since 1992.

"Since there was an overall resource constraint and as petrochemical projects were capital-intensive, the view prevailing then was that the public financial institutions may not be in a position to cater to the needs of other priority sectors if mega-petrochemical projects took away resources from them," it said.

The 11 large-scale projects which have been approved since 1989 were expected to be funded through either internal generation of resources, equity or borrowings from the capital market, the statement said.
"Since then, the situation has changed. Therefore, it is necessary that finance at competitive rates is available for such mega-projects and the ban should be lifted," the statement said.
